chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wore the shirt, he extended his hand; and when it reached the tips of the fingers, he cut it off.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What was the preferred length of the sleeves for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) meticulous adherence to the Sunnah of dress, specifically ensuring his sleeves did not hang loosely beyond the fingertips, a practice that distinguishes the Prophetic model from later cultural excesses. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ittiba’* (following the Imams) in daily habits, where even minor details of attire serve as manifestations of spiritual discipline and modesty. This specific measurement reflects the balance between practicality for action and the dignified restraint expected of the leader of the faithful.
